key_insight: No statevector simulator dominates: the fastest choice depends on qubit count, CPU threading, and GPU use.
engineering_relevance: Select simulation backends using absolute runtimes on target hardware rather than GPU-over-CPU speedup ratios alone.
method: Benchmarked Cirq (qsim), CUDA-Q, and Qiskit (Aer) on a Trotterized 2D quantum acoustic wave simulation.
Measured CPU and GPU runtimes across 7–29 qubits on one Azure virtual machine.
Evaluated CPU strong scaling at 27 qubits and GPU-over-CPU speedups.
evidence_signal: Qiskit sustained 80% CPU parallel efficiency at 16 threads, while Cirq's GPU backend was 1.5× faster than CUDA-Q and 2.3× faster than Qiskit at 29 qubits.
watch_item: Results are workload- and hardware-specific; CUDA-Q's 1500× GPU-over-CPU speedup at 21 qubits largely reflects limited scaling of its qpp CPU backend.
paper_title: Benchmark Study for Quantum Statevector Simulators for Scientific Computing
